title: September issue — check what stuck
intro: Eight self-check questions from the September 2026 issue.

questions.prompt: The four checks that actually matter, per the issue:
choices: Daily P&L, weekly rankings, NFO calendar, star ratings
Monthly contribution, allocation drift, genuine diversification underneath, and capital-gains tax building
Fund manager changes, expense ratios, exit loads, benchmarks
Whatever your app's home screen shows
questions.explanation: And they run on a yearly clock. The daily number is 'anxiety with a green-and-red interface' — feedback that arrives too fast produces action that is mostly noise.

choices: Fund selection is everything
How much you save matters far more than which fund you pick — contributions do the heavy lifting until the base can compound
Brilliant picking beats steady saving from day one
Returns don't matter at all
questions.explanation: The diligent saver beats the brilliant picker for years; the return advantage only matters once the base is large.

questions.prompt: Nifty 50 vs Nifty 50 Equal Weight over the past year:
choices: Identical returns — same stocks, same result
N50 −2.3% vs Equal Weight +8.2% — same 50 stocks, different weights
Equal Weight lost more because of small stocks
They hold different stocks
questions.explanation: Top 10 stocks are over half the Nifty 50; every group of ten is ~20% of the Equal Weight index. Weights, not names, set outcomes — and the arithmetic reverses when heavyweights lead.

questions.prompt: The small-cap category's three-year return after the slump:
choices: 15% a year — small caps always win eventually
5.5% a year — less than a liquid fund over the same period
Exactly zero
−13.2% a year
questions.explanation: −13.2% is the YTD figure. The three-year 5.5%/yr below liquid-fund returns is the number the rally hid: volatility that went unpaid.

questions.prompt: The IT fall (Nifty IT −41.5%) was primarily…
choices: An earnings collapse
A re-rating: ~28× earnings to under 17× while earnings rose — pricing the AI threat to billable-hours growth
A currency artifact only
Caused by SEBI rules
questions.explanation: Constant-currency growth at the big five ran low single digits — not what 28× was built on. And the AUM-weighted line above the median shows the largest funds held on more than the typical fund.

questions.prompt: Chollet's bubble framing, as the issue uses it:
choices: Bubbles only happen with fake technology
A bubble is a property of the people buying — possible even when the tech works and demand is real
AI cannot be a bubble
Bubbles are impossible in index funds
questions.explanation: Prices, not products, make bubbles. The frame applies to every hot theme in the magazine's pages.

choices: Add up everything you own and multiply by 25
First subtract the promised-away money (loans past retirement, weddings, parents' care) — the multiple applies only to what's actually yours
Ignore unwritten family obligations
Plan for exactly 35 years in all cases
questions.explanation: Commit a fifth of the corpus and 350× monthly expenses becomes ~438× on the rest — the correction rises faster than the committed share. Unwritten promises get collected as reliably as a bank's.

questions.prompt: Why does an early hospital bill hurt a retirement plan disproportionately?
choices: Hospitals charge retirees more
Early withdrawals lose the most compounding years — the corpus stays smaller for longest, and the income gap is widest just after the bill
It doesn't — timing is irrelevant
Because insurance never pays
questions.explanation: The shock correction: the gap closes only near the end of the plan. Protecting the early years is worth the most.
